operations.comment: ; Maintained local commentary; physical identities include the 16-byte iNES header.
; iNES header: eight 16 KiB PRG units, sixteen 8 KiB CHR units, mapper 1, no trainer. Header mirroring is
; a startup declaration; MMC1 controls working mirroring.
; Enter the existing display initializer with lower PRG slots [0,1]. This forwarding entry has
; ordinary JMP behavior.
; Frame entry jumps past initialization into palette, text, scroll and selected display updates.
; Set MMC1 control/CHR registers, hide sprites and clear display results. Double the display selector to
; call its initializer through an interleaved little-endian address table. The selector is not an
; established level number.
; Fourteen little-endian display initializer targets, indexed by twice the selector. Classified as a
; bounded dispatch table; handler meanings vary by display.
; Several selected displays start at vertical scroll $E0. Enable rendering/NMI, run the palette
; transition, then wait for a result or cancellation. The selected transition mode determines the
; ordinary update or fade-out path.
; Clear transition mode before testing the display-local latch and selecting the existing transition
; path.
; Poll cancellation and result bytes; result 4 ends this wait too. The classified fragment does not
; include every edge back into the frame loop.
; Return after choosing or preserving the transition mode.
; Upload the palette and service text. Select a special scroll writer for displays 4/12, otherwise use
; vertical scroll 0 or $E0. Transition mode runs fades; normal mode polls input and calls the selected
; update handler unless ending is pending.
; Poll the controller and use the display selector to fetch a two-byte update address. The table extent
; and omitted handler bodies are still structural research questions.
; 14 little-endian state-handler words selected under this routine's finite initialized state
; contract. The handler transitions and independently coherent first handler bound this storage. The
; state is a local dispatch index, not an unrestricted shared-memory value.
; Advance the wrapping display tick, then run the result handlers when the ending latch requests them.
; A newly pressed direction can also set the result mask through the independently supported prefix.
; When either newly pressed direction bit in $0C is set, store that mask in the shared display result;
; both paths join the existing update. No independent natural caller is asserted.
; Update the display result handlers. A newly pressed low button bit also writes the result latch.
; All displays except 12 prepare the next raster delay. Return to the fixed-bank caller.
; Select this display's CHR pair. The rest of this initializer is outside the classified fragment.
; Copy the 256-byte OAM template, clear formation state, initialize horizontal step -4, twelve
; remaining targets, column indices and opening countdown 200. The shared countdown starts at one and
; the final helper builds display text.
; Run the opening palette/scroll countdown first. While active, move the player, accept fire, animate
; targets, emit and move enemy shots, test collisions and rebuild occupied-column indices. No
; remaining targets or the shared failure latch selects display exit.
; Choose the update cadence from the remaining-target count. Move visible pieces horizontally; if any
; reaches the side margin, lower the formation four pixels and reverse the signed step. Crossing the
; bottom limit enters the common failure path.
; One cadence mask per remaining-target count; the movement consumer masks FrameCounter before
; advancing the formation. Values and exact storage stop before the next routine.
; Derive one of two tile-source words from frame count and target-count cadence. Distribute four tile
; values to each four-piece target group; coordinates and attributes remain unchanged.
; Per-count right-shift counts used before selecting one of the two formation animation source words.
; After the shared countdown reaches zero, choose a nonzero signed horizontal step from frame bits and
; start the crossing object at the corresponding screen edge. Leave an already active crossing object
; alone.
; Every fourth frame draw four pieces at the crossing object's X coordinate and advance it by its
; signed step. Outside the horizontal margin, clear the step and hide all four pieces.
; Every 32 frames inspect the selected column and first free shot slot. Spawn a shot below the lowest
; occupied target, choose its downward speed from frame bits, then alternate the allocation slot.
; Empty columns are skipped within the four-column list.
; Move the two active enemy shots downward by their stored speeds. At Y $D8 retire the shot and hide
; its sprite.
; Use held left/right bits to add -1 or +1 to all nine player-piece X positions, bounded by the
; leading piece at $08 and $E8.
; If the player-shot latch is clear, enqueue sound $24 and place the shot at the player origin plus
; four pixels horizontally.
; Move the active player shot upward two pixels per frame. Above Y $20 hide it and clear the active
; latch.
; Choose a directional animation pair using held input and a frame bit, then copy sixteen interleaved
; tile/attribute bytes into the player OAM pieces.
; Test the player's single-piece shot against thirteen four-piece target groups using the shared
; rectangle predicate. On a hit hide the target and shot, enqueue sound $18 and update the reward.
; Ordinary targets decrement the remaining count; the final crossing group instead clears its movement
; fields.
; Test two enemy shots against the player group. A hit hides the shot, replaces the player's nine-
; piece image relative to its current origin, latches failure and enqueues sound $19.
; For each of four columns, walk upward through target rows in $40-byte OAM steps until a visible
; group is found. Store its logical row/column selector, or zero when the column is empty.
; Four two-byte-spaced logical starting indices at CPU $8625, then four OAM source words at $862D. For
; each column the scanner subtracts $40 from the OAM pointer and four from the logical index until it
; finds a visible target or exhausts the column.
; Below 128 ticks select four palette bytes from the countdown. Between ticks 20 and 99 also use an
; eight-cell scroll shake and enqueue sound $28. Decrement the countdown each update.
; Sixteen palette bytes form four four-color rows selected by countdown bits; the final eight bytes at
; CPU $8682 are vertical-scroll shake values selected by countdown & 7.
; Use frame bits 5..6 to select one of four colors for palette byte $0310.
; Bounded repeated OAM tile/attribute records and pointer layers for this display. The 256-byte
; initialization template begins at CPU $8717; complete original grouping of the surrounding sprite
; backing remains unresolved.
; Copy 32 bytes of player sprite data and one extra sprite; clear five four-byte state slots and seed
; motion phases. Three slots spawn from the left and two from the right. Shared RAM is reused by other
; displays.
; Countdown initialization gates input and motion. Update player position/animation, two groups of moving
; sprite objects and collision tests; mark ending when a failure/result flag is set.
; After a cooldown, scan three four-byte slots for an inactive one. Resolve its sprite pointer, mark
; active, create eight sprites at the left edge and schedule a new cooldown.
; Five four-byte descriptors: little-endian OAM destination followed by two zero bytes. Object
; consumers index the pointer pair with byte offsets 0,4,8,12,16; the descriptor stride matches the
; local object-state stride.
; For three active slots, move eight sprite X coordinates using the slot's phase table. Retire a slot
; once its leading X reaches $F0. Omitted retirement bytes remain unknown.
; After an object leaves the screen, start its respawn delay when the left-side cooldown is clear,
; then hide all eight pieces through the selected OAM pointer.
; Scan five slots in state 2. Choose a sprite template from direction/state flags and copy via two
; pointers. Only the first copy operation is classified; its remaining fields and bounds are unresolved.
; Copy the remaining tile/attribute bytes for the hit image. On timer expiry hide all eight pieces,
; release the object slot and start the respawn cooldown when allowed.
; Held left/right moves the player sprite group one pixel inside the $08..$E7 boundary. Scratch delta is
; signed; all sprites share the displacement.
; Complete the four-byte OAM stride and stop after the eight player pieces have moved.
; Use held direction and frame phase to select tile bytes, then write them into the player OAM group. The
; classified fragment omits part of the copy loop.
; Copy the selected sprite's attribute byte, then advance the OAM stride and source until sixteen
; tile/attribute bytes are consumed.
; When no extra shot is active, place it at the player's Y and X+4 and set its active latch.
; When active, subtract three from the extra sprite Y; hide it at $F0 and clear its active flag above the
; upper boundary.
; Compare the extra sprite with five eight-sprite groups through the shared overlap helper. Advance the
; target pointer by $20 for each group; a hit begins hiding that group.
; Finish hiding the selected object pieces, select its hit state with a 30-frame timer and adjust the
; shared score according to template variant. Hide the shot and clear its active latch.
; Expand eight four-byte OAM records from a template: add supplied X/Y origins and optionally force
; attribute 2. The template order is Y,tile,attribute,X.
; Preserve the slot index while selecting a signed motion delta. Skip sprites hidden at Y=$F0 and adjust
; the X byte of this OAM record.
; Sixteen unsigned horizontal steps (1,2,3,2 in four-cell bands) indexed by the object's modulo-
; sixteen phase. The movement helper adds the selected value to each visible piece's X.
; Derive a $10..$2F frame cooldown from the shared frame counter.
; Advance the motion phase in five four-byte records modulo 16.
; After a separate cooldown, scan the last two slots. Build an eight-sprite object at X=$F0,Y=$28 with
; template attributes, then schedule the next spawn.
; Move the final two active groups using their motion phases. A leading X below 8 retires the group; part
; of that retirement path remains unknown.
; Start the right-side spawn delay when allowed, then hide all eight pieces through the selected OAM
; pointer.
; Derive a $20..$2F frame cooldown from the frame counter.
; Apply the right-group signed phase delta to an OAM record unless its Y is the hidden sentinel. Preserve
; the caller's slot index.
; Repeated sprite-piece records and pointer layers bounded by the preceding object helper and
; following initializer. Existing display consumers copy interleaved tile/attribute bytes and four-
; byte OAM pieces. Complete original grouping of the backing storage remains unresolved.
; Select the display's CHR pair; the remaining initializer is not yet classified.
; Hide sprites, copy two display OAM templates and clear the press counter plus four local state bytes
; before the common text initialization.
; Use local state $0526 in 0..3 to select four little-endian handler words. The initializer and
; handlers establish this conditional state contract.
; Four little-endian handler words indexed by ButtonCountPhase in 0..3. The initializer clears the
; phase; the active handler advances to completion and then exit.
; Wait for the common message/countdown helper to finish, start message selector 5 and advance to
; state 1.
; Wait for the message, then run the common display timer. For each accepted low-button press enqueue
; sound $2B and count the press; every fourth press increments the shared result. Update the selected
; OAM image and common result display; failure or timeout enters state 2.
; Wait for the common message/countdown helper. Compare the shared result with 20, load 6 or 7, then
; overwrite A with state 3. These intermediate values are not passed to a message helper here.
; Set the shared display-exit latch and return.
; Select one of two 80-byte OAM source blocks using bit 1 of the press counter and copy the complete
; selected block.
; Two source words at CPU $8E2D choose the 80-byte OAM block using press-counter bit 1. Repeated four-
; byte sprite cells supply Y,tile,attribute,X; the two bounded templates follow the pointer pair.
; Select the display's CHR pair; the remaining initializer is not yet classified.
; Copy the two player/obstacle OAM templates and place two four-piece obstacles. Initialize horizontal
; speeds -1 and -2, clear local activity/failure/direction/state and start the word timer before
; common text setup.
; Select four handlers using local state $052C in 0..3. Initialization and phase transitions establish
; the conditional domain.
; Four little-endian handler words selected by PairedJumpPhase in 0..3, established by the initializer
; and phase transitions.
; Wait for the common message/countdown helper, start message selector 8 and select active state 1.
; Wait for the message and run the common display timer. Update obstacle speed/animation and, until
; failure is latched, update jumping, player images, obstacle motion and both player collision groups.
; Common failure or timeout advances to state 2.
; Wait for the message helper, compare the result with 20 and load 6 or 7. The following state-3 load
; overwrites that value; no result-message call occurs in this block.
; Set the shared display-exit latch and return.
; While the shared jump latch is set, held left/right moves both player groups inside their horizontal
; bounds. Every fourth frame apply the signed Y profile to visible pieces and count down. A new low-
; button press starts a 25-step jump, increments the shared result and enqueues sound $26.
; Twenty-six signed Y deltas. Starting at index 25 the jump updater walks backward through indices
; 25..1 at one step per four frames, then clears the jump latch. Cell zero is stored but not read by
; this countdown path.
; For each player group choose an idle/jumping source pointer from the current horizontal direction,
; then copy sixteen tile/attribute bytes into its eight OAM pieces. Coordinates remain intact.
; Move the two four-piece obstacles horizontally by their signed speeds. Reverse a speed when its
; leading X coordinate leaves the $08..$E7 window.
; Use frame bit 1 to choose a four-piece source record, then copy its tile bytes to four obstacle OAM
; groups without changing their coordinates or attributes.
; With destination pointer in $07/$08 and origin X,Y, copy a four-piece template. Add Y to each source
; Y and X to each source X while preserving tile/attribute bytes. Entry requires a writable sixteen-
; byte destination; no natural caller is implied by the contract.
; Test the first player's group against two four-piece obstacles. On a hit latch failure, enqueue
; sound $19 and replace nine player pieces with the failure image relative to their current origin.
; Test the second player's group against the same two obstacles. On a hit set the common failure
; latches and replace that player's nine pieces with the failure image at its current origin.
; Select the right-facing image and add one to the X positions of both eight-piece player groups.
; Select the left-facing image and subtract one from the X positions of both eight-piece player
; groups.
; Decrement the word timer. On expiry reload it and increase each obstacle's speed magnitude by one
; while preserving its sign; arithmetic remains eight-bit.
; Load the little-endian countdown with $04B0 (1200 updates).
; Bounded pointer layers and interleaved sprite/OAM records consumed by the paired player and obstacle
; renderers. CPU $92CE/$92F2 and $9316/$933A supply idle/jumping source lists for the two facing
; directions. CPU $93A6 chooses obstacle animation, $93CA is a 48-byte OAM initialization block and
; $93FA a nine-piece failure image. The complete original storage grouping remains unresolved.
; Select CHR/control settings and copy a twelve-sprite player template. Seed four object records, player
; control state, scrolling counters and a secondary nine-sprite decoration.
; Wait for the start countdown, periodically queue sound from a speed-dependent frame mask, then update
; control, player sprites, scrolling, objects, collisions and palette cycling. A high scroll/result
; condition sets the ending request.
; Tail-call the shared display target updater after the preceding cadence test.
; Thirteen cadence-mask bytes consumed by the neighboring count-indexed display update. Values repeat
; $1F,$0F,$07,$03 bands; the consumer combines the mask with frame count. Original game-specific
; meaning of each count remains uncertain.
; Write the horizontal scroll counter and zero vertical scroll to the PPU latch pair.
; A recovery timer reduces speed toward $10. Otherwise up/down change a signed vertical control value by
; two; speed approaches its target while the control value damps toward zero.
; Convert signed control magnitude to a quarter-sized delta, keep the player within the vertical limits,
; and move twelve sprite Y coordinates. Derive a coarse speed index from the speed's upper nibble.
; Choose one of two twelve-tile frames from the frame counter and update only tile fields, keeping OAM
; stride four.
; Add the current horizontal step to the low counter, then add one plus carry to the high counter. This
; is the exact arithmetic; its high byte is also used as a progression flag.
; Copy the coarse speed index into the horizontal step byte.
; Apply the selected signed unit step (+1 or -1) to all twelve player OAM Y coordinates. Frame bits
; choose one of the two stored deltas.
; The two signed unit steps +1 and -1 selected by the neighboring direction consumer.
; Only run after scrolling enables object processing. Scan four four-byte records; inactive slots count
; down, state 2 resolves an object pointer and calls its update helper. Intermediate states and helper
; bodies remain unknown.
; When the selected object slot's countdown expires, activate it. Choose one of eight local
; directions, retain its direction flag and select a four-piece OAM destination. A random nibble
; offsets the spawn Y; construct the appropriate sprite at X $F0 and restore the object index before
; the common continuation.
; Apply the paired coordinate adjustments to selected pieces. On countdown expiry release the slot,
; choose a new cooldown from frame bits and hide all four pieces.
; Four four-byte descriptors give OAM destination word and Y base, followed by eight local variant
; flags. Object index selects a descriptor in four-byte strides; a separately masked random value
; selects the variant flag.
; For four object groups, subtract scroll speed from four X bytes. State 1 objects crossing the left edge
; are hidden. Each group occupies sixteen bytes of OAM and four bytes of state.
; Hide the remaining three OAM pieces, release the selected object slot and choose a new bounded
; cooldown from frame bits.
; Use X,Y as origin and $07/$08 as writable sixteen-byte OAM destination. Copy four Y,tile,attribute,X
; cells from the local source; add the origin only to coordinates.
; Copy the alternative four-piece source at origin X,Y. When input A is 2 force each attribute to 3;
; otherwise preserve the source attributes. Destination pointer must address sixteen writable bytes.
; Use a four-step frame phase to replace one palette-buffer byte. Palette colors remain in the unknown
; ROM table.
; Four palette colors selected by the four-step frame phase and written to the scrolling display's
; palette buffer.
; Compare the player bounds against four sixteen-byte groups. A hit sets the matching object to state
; 2 with a ten-tick response count. Variant zero starts the special timer/sound; variant two extends
; the timer, increments the shared score and queues its sound.
; Set a ten-tick object response countdown. Variant zero latches a special timer and sound $2A;
; variant two sets a longer timer, increments the shared result and enqueues sound $2B. Other variants
; simply return through the existing continuation.
; At caller-selected Y, subtract two unless the byte is the hidden-sprite sentinel $F0. Pointer and
; coordinate selection are caller preconditions.
; At caller-selected Y, add two unless the byte is $F0. Pointer and coordinate selection are caller
; preconditions.
; Copy 36 bytes into nine consecutive OAM records.
; Bounded sprite templates and little-endian tile-source pointers for the scrolling display.
; Initialization copies a twelve-piece player template and nine-piece secondary image; runtime helpers
; select interleaved tile/attribute bytes and place four-piece objects. Full original container
; grouping remains unresolved.
; Select CHR banks; remaining initializer bytes are unknown.
; Clear cue/player/opponent activity and phase, start the cue delay at 120 and initialize common
; display text.
; Select four phase handlers using local phase $057E in 0..3. Initialization and the active-to-finish-
; to-exit transitions establish the conditional domain.
; 4 little-endian state-handler words selected under this routine's finite initialized state contract.
; The handler transitions and independently coherent first handler bound this storage. The state is a
; local dispatch index, not an unrestricted shared-memory value.
; Wait for the common message/countdown helper, start selector 2 and advance to phase 1.
; After the message finishes, run the common display timer, cue state, both response timers/images,
; score resolution and alternating OAM copies. Shared failure or timeout selects phase 2.
; Wait for the common message/countdown helper and compare the two shared scores. The loaded values
; 3/4 are overwritten by the phase-3 load here; no message helper consumes them in this block.
; Set the common display-exit latch.
; Count down the active cue and reset to a 40-tick idle delay. On idle expiry choose cue 1 or 2 and a
; 50-tick active window. Compute the opponent response threshold from the remaining timer and frame
; bits, biased by the current score difference; cue 2 can suppress that threshold.
; For nonzero cue choose one of two sixteen-byte OAM sources and copy four complete pieces. With no
; cue hide all four pieces.
; A new low-button press starts a 40-tick player response latch. While active count down to zero and
; release it.
; Copy the 44-byte active response image into scratch OAM, or hide its eleven pieces by setting their
; Y bytes to $F0.
; Count down active response or its six-tick recovery. When a cue exists and its timer has crossed the
; stored threshold, start a 40-tick opponent response.
; Copy the 28-byte active response image into scratch OAM, or hide its seven pieces. The later
; display-copy helper copies forty bytes from this scratch area, including adjacent backing bytes.
; Only the first tick of a new player/opponent response can score against the active cue. Cue 1
; increments that participant's score; cue 2 decrements it with saturation at zero. Consuming a
; response clears the cue and resets its delay to 40.
; On alternating frames swap which forty-byte scratch image is copied first into OAM groups $0724 and
; $0750. This changes draw priority; the copy counts remain forty bytes even though the opponent's
; initialized image has only 28 bytes.
; A 44-byte player response image and 28-byte opponent image are followed by two cue-source words and
; two sixteen-byte four-piece cue images. The scratch-to-OAM helper copies forty bytes from each
; participant's scratch area; the opponent's initialized 28-byte image does not by itself explain the
; extra twelve bytes read there.
; Forward this selector's initialization to a shared CHR setup entry.
; Tail-call the common parity-choice phase dispatcher from this display update slot.
; Select the display CHR pair, then initialize the common parity-choice state, countdown and OAM pair
; before text setup. Several initializer slots share this fragment.
; Set the local selection limit to 15, clear phase/pair/choice-result state, start a 180-update
; countdown, draw the selected pair and initialize common text.
; Select eight little-endian phase targets using initialized local state 0..7. Each selected handler
; updates the same field; this is a conditional local contract.
; 8 little-endian state-handler words selected under this routine's finite initialized state contract.
; The handler transitions and independently coherent first handler bound this storage. The state is a
; local dispatch index, not an unrestricted shared-memory value.
; Wait for the message helper, start selector 9, advance to phase 1 and clear the player's even/odd
; choice offset.
; After the message, a new low-button press starts selector $10, phase 4 and a cleared choice offset.
; While the 180-update countdown is nonzero, animate the pair and decrement it. Expiry selects phase
; Compute the parity of the two chosen values, compare it with the player's choice offset, select
; message $0A/$0B and latch its boolean result. Both paths select phase 5.

; Unknown physical $01C99..$01C9A: Structural role or exact instruction/data boundary remains unresolved. Raw bytes are retained at the exact physical bounds; neighboring routines do not extend across this interval.
; After the message, update the left/right choice image. A new low-button press restarts phase 2 with
; countdown 180 and sound $1F.
; When the message helper finishes, set both timeout/failure and exit latches.
; Hide the choice sprite, compute the pair parity and select message $0C/$0D, then phase 7.
; A newly pressed low button selects phase 3.
; Generate two random indices by shifting and masking the shared random helper's result. Use the
; eight-byte value table to store the two even source offsets.
; Eight stored even offsets 0,0,2,4,6,8,10,10. Random low three bits index this table, so the
; duplicated endpoints bias the six source choices.
; Resolve one four-piece source word for each selected offset, drawing at Y $A8 with X origins $6C and
; $84 into the two sixteen-byte OAM destinations.
; Copy four Y,tile,attribute,X cells through source and destination pointers. Add scratch Y/X origin
; bytes to coordinates, preserving tile and attribute.
; Every fourth frame randomize the pair and redraw it; otherwise return without changing its image.
; Divide each even source offset by two, add them plus two, and return bit zero of the sum.
; New left/right presses choose offset 0 or 2. Copy the corresponding four-byte OAM cursor cell to
; Hide the choice cursor by storing the $F0 Y sentinel.
; Bounded four-piece source records, their little-endian pointer layer and two cursor cells. Selected
; even offsets identify a source word; the four-piece copy adds the caller's origin to Y and X and
; preserves tile/attribute bytes. Full original container grouping remains unresolved.
; Copy two twelve-sprite groups; seed four small sprite records, activity flags, direction deltas and a
; spawn cooldown. Finish with common HUD/collision/sound initialization.
; After the start countdown, update player movement/animation, opposing group motion, small falling
; objects, multiplexed sprites and collisions, then refresh HUD digits and request ending on a result
; flag.
; A newly pressed A button sets a short special state. Held horizontal input moves twelve sprite X
; coordinates by signed two within the screen limits; idle clears the movement state.
; Finish the four-byte OAM stride, stopping after twelve pieces.
; Select idle, moving or special-state tile/attribute pairs according to facing. Moving animation uses
; the frame phase. Copy twelve pairs into OAM with stride four.
; Wait for a cooldown, then choose motion from the opposing sprite's X limits or the shared pseudo-random
; helper. The central selection path is not completely classified.
; Finish the random state-bit choice, then use random carry to choose signed step +2 or -2. Pass it
; through the score-dependent bias helper, store it and choose a 20..51-frame countdown.
; Store the selected horizontal step, select motion state 1 and choose a 25..56-frame countdown from
; frame bits.
; Move twelve sprite X coordinates by a signed direction delta, honoring left/right screen limits.
; Use direction and a frame-derived two-state index to choose twelve tile/attribute pairs for the
; opposing group.
; Alternate two eight-byte source groups between OAM positions on odd/even frames. This shares sprite
; slots across four small records; the first parity path is only partly classified.
; Advance the source index and stop after sixteen selected tile bytes.
; For four two-byte slots mix a random byte with a per-slot mask. On a zero result set a small nonzero
; vertical step, resolve the slot OAM pointer and initialize Y=0 with a random X inside the slot's
; base range.
; Resolve the selected OAM pointer, start its Y at zero and choose an X offset from random low six
; bits plus the slot's base. Continue into the existing object-state update.
; Four mask/X-base pairs at CPU $A11A, followed by four little-endian OAM pointers at $A122. Even slot
; offsets select the corresponding mask and base; accepted activation initializes Y to zero and X to
; random low six bits plus that base.
; For active two-byte state slots, resolve an OAM pointer and add the vertical step to the first sprite
; Y. Later movement/retirement operations are outside the classified fragment.
; At Y $A8 or below clear the selected object's active field and hide its OAM Y byte.
; Only the player's negative special state tests collisions. Facing chooses a player sub-sprite; compare
; against four four-byte small-object records, skipping inactive slots.
; A zero rectangle-predicate result enters the existing player-hit continuation; other results keep
; scanning.
; Hide the selected object, release its slot, increment the player's score and enqueue sound $2B.
; Gate collision checks on two HUD counters and animation phase. Choose an opponent sub-sprite by facing
; and compare with the active small-object records.
; A zero rectangle-predicate result enters the existing opponent-hit continuation; other results keep
; scanning.
; Hide the selected object, release its slot and increment the opponent's score.
; Return 0 or 2 from the shared frame phase, suitable for a little-endian pointer table.
; Preserve input A while comparing the two scores. When the player leads by at least four, adjust the
; restored signed step by +2 or -2 according to its sign; otherwise return A unchanged. The sign mask
; is the following code byte $80, not a separate extended table.
; Bounded repeated OAM pieces, coordinate/pointer layers and sprite tile/attribute backing consumed by
; the neighboring display graph. Exact internal container grouping and natural selection of every
; stored row remain unresolved.
; Reuse the shared initializer fragment. The full behavior is not yet classified.
; Tail-call the common parity-choice phase dispatcher from this alternate display update slot.
; Reuse the shared initializer fragment. The full behavior is not yet classified.
; Tail-call the common parity-choice phase dispatcher from this second alternate display update slot.

; Unknown physical $02400..$02401: Structural role or exact instruction/data boundary remains unresolved. Raw bytes are retained at the exact physical bounds; neighboring routines do not extend across this interval.
; Write MMC1 control value $1E and select CHR banks; the latter operation continues into unknown bytes.
; Hide sprites and copy the main, secondary and extra OAM templates. Clear local state and initialize
; a choice cursor, word timers and phase fields; an enabled alternate mode starts with choice 1.
; Initialize common text last.
; Clear the left-edge rendering mask bits, apply top scroll, burn a 16-bit delay and decrement a separate
; timer. A new Start press enables the alternate mode. Run the state-selected update and prepare the next
; delay.
; Call the existing four-byte choice-cursor renderer in this update path.
; Busy-wait until the 16-bit delay reaches zero, reset scroll, then select PPU control $90/$91 according
; to the alternate-mode flag. Timing intent is inferred from the PPU writes, not verified scanline
; accuracy.
; Write horizontal scroll and zero vertical scroll; the low bit of the high scroll counter selects the
; nametable in PPUCTRL.
; Double the local phase and select one of five little-endian handlers under phase 0..4. The
; initializer and approach/crossing/return/departure transitions establish the conditional domain.
; 5 little-endian state-handler words selected under this routine's finite initialized state contract.
; The handler transitions and independently coherent first handler bound this storage. The state is a
; local dispatch index, not an unrestricted shared-memory value.
; While the timer high byte is nonzero, move the eight-sprite group downward toward its Y threshold.
; Otherwise move it horizontally on alternate frames. A zero timer advances the state to 1.
; Finish the four-byte stride and stop after eight pieces.
; Skip while the high timer bit is set. Animate the main group, move it left inside the margin and
; advance the local word counter. When that counter reaches its phase boundary, select state 2, signed
; backing timer -256 and a new countdown.
